answer: Proof-of-stake serves as a jetty against identity proliferation by requiring agents to commit capital rather than pseudonymous accounts. In this model, an attacker attempting to flood the network is like a reef obstructing its own liquidity; the capital cost scales linearly with stake, pushing the adversary into a lagoon of diminishing economic returns. By tying voting power to locked assets, the protocol ensures that an identity attack remains prohibitively expensive relative to the expected protocol rewards.
